artworks.title: The Building of the Trojan Horse
artworks.description: Tiepolo's National Gallery canvas: Epeius' carpenters raise Athena's stratagem outside the walls — the horse still hollow and unfinished.

artworks.title: The Procession of the Trojan Horse into Troy
artworks.description: The procession into Troy — Tiepolo's companion scene of the gift the city pulls through its own gates.

artworks.title: Child Murder (Mykonos Vase, detail)
artworks.description: The Mykonos pithos — among the earliest images of the Trojan Horse, and of the massacre that follows when the belly opens.

artworks.title: The Greek Sinon before Priam
artworks.description: Sinon before Priam: the captive whose false tale persuades Troy to accept the horse — the verbal half of the stratagem.

films.title: Troy
films.description: Petersen's epic made the hollow horse and the night of fire the defining Trojan image for a generation.

films.title: Helen of Troy
films.description: Wise's peplum keeps Sinon, Laocoön, and the horse entering the gates — mid-century Hollywood's sack prelude.

popCulture.title: Trojan Horse
popCulture.description: The gift that opens a city remains the archetype of infiltration — and the proverb for malware that arrives as software.

popCulture.title: Aeneid
popCulture.creator: Virgil
popCulture.description: Book II — Sinon's speech, Laocoön's warning, and Aeneas watching the horse bring Troy's end from within.

popCulture.title: Little Iliad
popCulture.description: The cyclic poem of the horse's building — Epeius, Odysseus' counsel, and the warriors hidden in the belly.
